fatal_errors: The hypothesis does not identify the target material, Re-containing Nb20Mo20Ta20W20Re20 refractory high-entropy-alloy film.
It replaces the studied Re addition to NbMoTaW with unsupported nickel or manganese additions to pure iron.
It omits helium implantation, irradiation-induced hardening, grain-boundary embrittlement, and the room-temperature thin-film conditions central to the target.
The proposed slip/dislocation mechanism does not reconstruct the observed defect-sink, amorphous-boundary, and helium-bubble-suppression mechanism.
The pure-iron elongation baseline is uncited, condition-dependent, and unrelated to the study baseline; describing copper as a low-ductility pure metal is also misleading.
explanation: The response addresses ductility only in a generic sense. It neither reconstructs the NbMoTaW versus NbMoTaWRe comparison nor explains why Re-containing films better resist helium-induced boundary embrittlement. Its tensile-test proposal could test a separate iron-alloying claim, but it does not discriminate the target mechanism or outcome and uses an overly broad falsification rule.
